title: Christian Living - Episode 5: Content in Every Season

parts.speaker: David
parts.style: cheerful for a brand new guest, a big smile in the voice, but speaking slowly at a relaxed pace, then settling into a calm bedtime tone
parts.text: Hello again, and welcome back to the SleepFit podcast series. <short pause> This is Christian Living, episode five: Content in Every Season. <chuckle> I'm David Lee, and tonight, I'm not alone. <short pause> I'm joined by a friend who's agreed to stay up a little past her bedtime. Maya, welcome. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.style: warm, relaxed, unhurried, a soft smile in the voice
parts.text: Thanks, David. <chuckle> It's good to be here. Hello, everyone. I'm Maya Brooks. <short pause> And I promise to keep my voice nice and sleepy. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.style: warm, relaxed, unhurried, a soft smile in the voice
parts.text: Perfect. <short pause> Tonight, we're asking a question that touches every season of life... <short pause> how do we find contentment, when circumstances keep changing? <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: That's a big one. <short pause> I think most of us are waiting for the day when things finally settle down... and then we'll feel content. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: And that's exactly where Paul surprises us. <short pause> He wrote to the Philippians... from prison. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: From prison. <short pause> So he wasn't sitting in a comfortable chair, offering theories about contentment. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: No. He was in a cell... and yet he'd discovered something most of us spend our whole lives searching for. <short pause> Listen. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: Learned. <short pause> I love that word. <short pause> It means contentment isn't something we're born with. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: It doesn't come naturally to any of us. <short pause> We're born wanting, reaching, comparing. <short pause> A child sees another child's toy, and immediately wants it... even if a moment before, they were perfectly happy with their own. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.style: warm, relaxed, unhurried, a soft smile in the voice
parts.text: <chuckle> I've watched that happen in my own kitchen. <short pause> And if we're honest, we carry that into adulthood. <short pause> Just with bigger toys. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.style: warm, relaxed, unhurried, a soft smile in the voice
parts.text: Bigger toys. <chuckle> But notice what Paul says he learned contentment in. <short pause> Not just in want... but in plenty, too. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: Now, that's the part I think we miss. <short pause> We understand that it takes grace to be content when we don't have enough. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: When life is hard. When prayers seem unanswered. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: But plenty can be just as dangerous to contentment. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: It can. <short pause> When we have abundance, we're tempted to think our security comes from what we own. <short pause> Our bank account. Our health. Our reputation. Our carefully built life. <short pause> And the moment those are threatened... our contentment vanishes. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: So Paul's secret has to be something that doesn't change when circumstances do. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: Exactly. He found his sufficiency in Christ. <short pause> And it wasn't a technique, or a mental trick. <short pause> It wasn't pretending that hardship doesn't hurt... <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: Or that blessings don't matter. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: Right. The secret was Christ's strength... available in every circumstance. <short pause> And Paul puts it like this. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.style: warm, relaxed, unhurried, a soft smile in the voice
parts.text: Okay, David, I have to say something about this one. <short pause> That verse is on so many mugs, and posters, and sports jerseys. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.style: warm, relaxed, unhurried, a soft smile in the voice
parts.text: <chuckle> It is. And it's often pulled out of its context, as if Christ will help us achieve any goal we set. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: But look at what Paul actually means by all things. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: To be content when he's hungry, and when he's full. <short pause> When he has nothing, and when he has plenty. <short pause> That's the victory he's describing. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: So Christ doesn't necessarily change our circumstances. <short pause> He strengthens us to be faithful within them. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: A heart that stays steady... when everything around us is shifting. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: <exhales> So, for anyone listening tonight... maybe you're in a season of want. <short pause> There's something you've needed for a long time. Something you've prayed for... and it hasn't come. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: The bank account stays low. The relationship stays broken. The health issue remains. The loneliness continues. <short pause> Paul doesn't minimize that pain. <short pause> But he shows us where to look. <short pause> Not at the empty place... but at Christ, who is present in it. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: Or maybe you're in a good season. Things are stable, and blessed. <short pause> And the temptation is to loosen your grip on Christ... and coast. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: Abundance needs contentment, too. <short pause> A learned discipline... of holding blessings with open hands. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: And contentment doesn't mean we stop caring about our circumstances. Or that we never work to change them. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: It means our peace isn't held hostage by them. <short pause> We can be fully present in this moment, this season, this day... because Christ is our sufficiency. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: And we don't learn it alone. <short pause> We learn it again in each new season... and Christ is the one who strengthens us. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: And his strength is enough. <short pause> Thank you, Maya, for being with me tonight. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.style: warm, relaxed, unhurried, a soft smile in the voice
parts.text: Thank you, David. It was lovely. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: Let's pray together. <long pause> Father, teach us contentment in this season, whatever it holds. <short pause> Help us find our sufficiency in Christ... not in what we have, or don't have. <long pause>

parts.speaker: Maya
parts.text: Rest well, everyone. <short pause> Goodnight. <long pause>

parts.speaker: David
parts.text: Goodnight.
